belongs_to: 'How can one construct a square having double the area of a given square?' (the given square drawn beside the question)

belongs_to: 'A first guess might be to simply double the length of each side... new square will have area 2 x 2 = 4 times the area of the original square'

LEFT: the original small square (side s), solid outline, one tick at the midpoint of its right side and one tick at the midpoint of its bottom side. RIGHT: a square with side 2s (twice the width and twice the height of the small one, so it is about 2 times as wide and tall), solid outline, vertically centred level with the small square; a dashed vertical line and a dashed horizontal line through its centre split it into 4 equal quarter squares, each the size of the small square. Ticks on the big square: the left side has 2 ticks (at the midpoint of its upper half and at the midpoint of its lower half), the bottom side has 2 ticks (midpoint of its left half and midpoint of its right half); the top and right sides have no ticks.

belongs_to: 'As Baudhayana says, the key is to construct a square on the diagonal of the original square' / 'Why does the new dotted square have double the area of the original square?'
description: A solid-outline square (original, side s) with its diagonal from the top-left vertex to the bottom-right vertex drawn dashed. A dashed square tilted 45 degrees (diamond orientation) is built on that diagonal, lying up and to the right of the original: its vertices are the original's top-left vertex (left vertex of the diamond), the original's bottom-right vertex (bottom vertex of the diamond), a top vertex directly above the original's top-right vertex at height s above the top edge, and a right vertex directly to the right of the original's top-right vertex at distance s. So the diamond's side equals the original's diagonal. No letters, numbers or ticks.

belongs_to: 'You could draw some horizontal and vertical lines as shown on the right' (east-west and north-south lines)
description: Same figure as the previous one with the horizontal and vertical lines added. Solid-outline original square (side s) at lower left; its diagonal (top-left to bottom-right) dashed; the dashed diamond on that diagonal (vertices: original's top-left vertex, original's bottom-right vertex, a top vertex at s above the original's top-right vertex, a right vertex at s to the right of that vertex). Added dashed lines: a dashed horizontal line continuing the original's top edge to the right, from the original's top-right corner to the right vertex of the diamond; a dashed vertical line continuing the original's right edge upward, from the original's top-right corner to the top vertex of the diamond. These two lines meet at the original's top-right corner, which is the centre of the diamond, and cut the diamond into 4 equal right triangles (the original square holds 2 of them, split by its dashed diagonal; the other 2 lie outside it at top and right). No letters or numbers.

belongs_to: 'Adding some more horizontal and vertical lines can make the situation even clearer' (the 4 + 4 congruent triangles figure)
description: A square of side 2s (outer square) with the original square of side s as its LOWER-LEFT quarter. Outline: the top side, the right side, the upper half of the left side and the right half of the bottom side are DASHED; the lower half of the left side and the left half of the bottom side (the original square's own left and bottom edges) are SOLID. A solid horizontal line runs through the centre from the left side to the right side and a solid vertical line runs through the centre from the top side to the bottom side (4 equal quarter squares). A dashed diamond joins the 4 midpoints of the outer sides (top-mid, right-mid, bottom-mid, left-mid); its lower-left dashed side is the diagonal of the original square. This makes 8 small congruent right triangles in all: 4 inside the diamond (cut by the cross) and 4 corner triangles outside it. Tick marks: one single short tick at the midpoint of each half-side of the outer square (8 single ticks: 2 on top, 2 on bottom, 2 on left, 2 on right, i.e. at 1/4 and 3/4 of each side). Each of the 4 dashed diamond sides carries a double tick mark (two short parallel slanted strokes) at its midpoint (4 double ticks), showing those 4 sides are equal. No letters or numbers.
